DesiredGainR critical re-audit — 1 August 2026

Source: AUDIT-2026-08-01.md

Superseded historical audit. This report describes the package snapshot reviewed on 1 August 2026. Its scientific release blockers were subsequently corrected in the current 0.5.0 source. It is retained only as an auditable record of the remediation process; use MATURITY.md, NEWS.md and inst/validation/ for the current evidence and readiness assessment.

Executive verdict

The new snapshot is materially better than the 31 July version. It resolves most of the earlier mechanical and simulation-contract findings and expands the test suite from 545 to 696 passing expectations. The package source builds and all six vignettes render.

It is nevertheless not release-ready and not yet safe to present as an expert-validated quantitative-genetics implementation. The ordinary source package check has one error, the CRAN-style check has two errors, the new no-skip CI job is guaranteed to fail, and three newly advertised scientific capabilities do not implement what their documentation says:

  1. DGSI’s default holdout selection uses rows that already influenced every fitted replicate;
  2. Mallard’s claimed absolute response constraint constrains unnormalised G b, not the actual response i G b / sqrt(b' P b), while the method labelled Harville is not Harville’s proportionality method; and
  3. residual covariance draws in propagate_covariance_uncertainty() are never passed to the simulation.

These are scientific validity issues, not polish.

Evidence collected

  • R 4.5.0 on Windows 11.
  • AlphaSimR 2.1.0 and ASRgenomics 1.1.6 installed.
  • devtools::test(): 696 pass, 0 fail, 0 warning, 3 skip.
  • Source tarball: built successfully with all six vignettes.
  • R CMD check --no-manual: 1 ERROR.
  • R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual: 2 ERRORs, 3 NOTES.
  • The check errors are reproducible and arise from the run_dgsi() example.
  • Both guide editions ship and resolve; the PDF renders cleanly over 17 pages.
  • Independent numerical probes reproduced the Mallard response error, the unnamed DGSI direction, and the checkpoint fingerprint collision.
  • The three CRAN-style notes observed locally were environmental: offline URL checks, inability to verify the clock, and Pandoc not inherited by one check subprocess. They are not counted as package defects here.

Release blockers

R1. R CMD check fails in the run_dgsi() example

The example at R/run_dgsi.R:139-168 generates candidate data whose estimated phenotypic covariance is incompatible with the supplied G. The new guard correctly stops, but the package’s own documented example therefore fails:

smallest eigenvalue of P - G is -0.586 against a sampling threshold of -0.378

Fix: supply a compatible named P in the example, or generate ref_data from a covariance that is admissible with G. Do not set the override merely to make the check pass. Require a clean standard and CRAN-style check before release, then correct cran-comments.md, which currently claims 0/0/0.

R2. The default DGSI “holdout” is data leakage

Every stochastic replicate is optimized on all rows at R/run_dgsi.R:521-566. Only after fitting finishes are holdout_rows sampled and used to choose among those already fitted replicates at lines 584-618. The comment at line 583 that the rows “played no part in producing” the coefficients is therefore false.

The guide, Rd page, NEWS and returned optimism$note all call this unbiased. It is not. Changing the alleged holdout observations can change the fitted coefficients before holdout scoring.

Fix: split before optimization. Fit all replicate searches on the training rows and choose among them on untouched validation rows. If coefficients are then refitted on all data, report the post-selection fit separately and do not call its objective an unbiased performance estimate. External validation_data should be allowed to select the replicate, not merely assess the winner chosen elsewhere.

Also update print.desired_gain_index(): it always says the result is the biased minimum over replicates even when the object claims a holdout rule.

R3. The newly advertised restricted-index families are not all valid

Mallard

The code enforces C G b = target and stores that quantity as achieved_response. Actual expected response is

i G b / sqrt(b' P b).

Because index scale is arbitrary, constraining unnormalised G b cannot impose an absolute response. In an independent probe, targets (0.4, 0.1) produced stored “achieved” values (0.4, 0.1) but actual expected responses (0.995227, 0.248807). The existing test checks only their ratio, despite its title claiming absolute responses.

Fix: remove the absolute-gain claim unless the normalized nonlinear constraint is solved with a stated selection intensity. Rename the current calculation as an unnormalised direction constraint if retained.

Harville

The implementation defines an arbitrary shrinkage penalty / (1 + penalty) between unrestricted and zero-response coefficients. Harville’s 1975 paper is Index selection with proportionality constraints, not a generic soft-penalty method. The package therefore attaches a historical name and citation to a locally invented regularization rule.

The citation is also wrong: the paper was authored by C. D. Kemp and D. A. Harville and its DOI is 10.2307/2529722; paper/paper.bib omits Kemp and uses 10.2307/2529724.

Fix: implement and verify the published proportionality formulation, or rename the current method without attributing it to Harville. Add coefficient and response checks against an independent reference implementation.

R4. Residual covariance uncertainty is drawn and then ignored

draw_covariance_pairs() correctly constructs G*, E* and P*. However, propagate_covariance_uncertainty() rebuilds the setup with only drawn$G at R/covariance_uncertainty.R:244-259; neither drawn$E nor drawn$P is ever used. AlphaSimR residual variance is instead recreated from the fixed h2. Consequently, changing P or residual_df does not propagate the advertised residual uncertainty through the simulation.

Fix: provide the drawn residual covariance to the phenotype-generation model, or remove P/residual_df and describe the function as genetic- covariance-only sensitivity analysis. Add a test proving that two different residual models change the distribution while holding the genetic draws fixed.

R5. The new full-dependency CI job must fail by construction

The workflow stops if any test skips. With every dependency and both guide editions installed, the current suite still skips:

  • the test of behavior when exactly one guide edition is absent;
  • the test of behavior when an optional dependency is absent; and
  • the complementary guide-edition condition.

This exact local configuration produced three skips. The workflow at .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:111-132 will therefore never pass.

Fix: separate dependency-required tests from intentional absence/edition branch tests. In the full-dependency job, run a tagged subset that must not skip, or turn mutually exclusive branch checks into direct unit tests using mocked paths/dependency availability.

High-priority correctness issues

H1. Checkpoint fingerprints are neither complete nor collision-resistant

digest_of() keeps only the first 4,096 serialized bytes and concatenates byte values without a cryptographic hash (R/optimize_desired_gains.R:93-102). A change late in a 100 x 100 founder haplotype matrix produced an identical fingerprint in an independent probe.

The fingerprint also omits mode-specific inputs such as economic_weights, target_gains, focal_trait and gain_floors, plus candidate-pool settings.

Fix: hash the complete serialized objects with a stable digest and include all scientific and search inputs. Add tests changing the first and last founder locus and every objective parameter individually.

H2. Optimizer Monte Carlo uncertainty is still handled incorrectly

Replicate outcomes and their covariance are computed by .dgr_evaluate_direction(), but only means and marginal standard errors are stored. Replicates and covariance are discarded.

.dgr_scalarised_error() then uses the mean marginal error for economic, target and constrained modes. That is not the uncertainty of:

  • w' outcome in economic mode;
  • the nonlinear target distance in target mode; or
  • the focal trait in constrained mode.

Repeated directions are evaluated with the same base seeds, yet the pooling code treats those identical runs as independent replication and shrinks the standard error. Frontier resampling also perturbs objectives and directions independently despite shared seeds and within-direction covariance.

Fix: retain replicate-level outcomes, scalarize each replicate under the actual mode, and estimate the scalar variance directly. Use new seeds for intentional replication. Preserve within- and across-direction common-random- number covariance when estimating frontier membership.

H3. The optimizer can enter a non-terminating loop

After the initial design, proposals come from a fixed n_candidates pool. Once all pool directions are excluded, every acquisition value is -Inf, which.max() returns an already evaluated point, its result is pooled, and the number of unique evaluated directions does not increase. The loop condition at line 590 remains true forever.

This is reachable when budget exceeds the number of unique initial plus pool directions; no validation prevents it.

Fix: validate the maximum unique budget, stop when no finite acquisition remains, or generate new candidate pools adaptively. Add a tiny-pool regression test.

H4. DGSI optimized directions lose their trait names

stats::rnorm() at R/run_dgsi.R:539 returns an unnamed proposal. When such a proposal improves the objective, optimised_d is stored unnamed. The new summary.desired_gain_index() indexes it by trait name, producing an absent or empty Optimised_gain column. This was reproduced independently.

Fix: restore names(proposal) <- trait_cols, and make summary() validate the object schema rather than silently accepting a length-zero lookup.

H5. Estimated-P compatibility allowance is unit-dependent

The sampling allowance is

-2 * sqrt(p / n) * max(diag(P)).

It compares the smallest raw eigenvalue of P - G with the largest marginal variance. This changes under a harmless rescaling of one trait. For example, P = diag(10000, 1) and G = diag(10000, 2) is accepted within the allowance, whereas expressing the first trait in units 100 times smaller makes the same biological pair inadmissible.

Fix: assess the residual in a standardized/generalized-eigenvalue space, or use a bootstrap/sampling distribution tied to the covariance estimator. Retain the strict stop, but make its tolerance invariant to trait units.

H6. Covariance-propagation summaries are mislabeled or fragile

  • point_estimate is the average across covariance draws, not an evaluation under setup$G_target.
  • rank_churn ranks the row mean of objectives in their raw units. That is unit-dependent and undefined as a preference for a Pareto problem.
  • n_replicates = 1 is allowed but produces all-NA Monte Carlo variances and can fail when choosing the “dominant” source.
  • One supplied direction is allowed, but dimension dropping can pass a vector to .dgr_non_dominated(), which expects a matrix.
  • The exported propagation function has no direct tests; existing tests cover only covariance-pair generation.

Fix: evaluate the original setup explicitly, require a declared scalarization for rank churn, handle or reject one replicate, preserve matrix dimensions, and add end-to-end tests.

H7. Diversity defaults remain internally incompatible and too permissive

founder_population() defaults to no marker panel, while optimize_desired_gains() defaults to include_diversity = TRUE. The default optimizer call therefore errors on a default setup.

On an AlphaSimR version where QTL-marker disjointness cannot be verified, the optimizer only warns and continues even though the resulting diversity axis may contain loci under selection. The covariance-propagation function checks only that a panel exists and does not check marker_qtl_overlap at all.

Fix: default diversity to FALSE, or create a verified panel by default. Require marker_qtl_overlap == FALSE unless the caller supplies an explicit experimental override recorded in provenance.

H8. Multi-environment stability is described as appended but is not usable

include_stability = TRUE returns a separate stability list. It does not append variables to labels, G, P or economic_weights, and restricted_index() accepts only trait selectors, not the arbitrary contrast matrix returned here. Thus the guide’s claim that stability contrasts can be passed into the existing index workflow is not implemented.

widen_environments() also silently takes the first record when a genotype has duplicate rows within an environment.

Fix: either return a fully augmented, usable index problem or provide an API that consumes the contrast matrix. Reject duplicate genotype-environment keys before widening. Label 1 - mean(environment correlation) as a heuristic, not an exact interaction-variance share for every correlation structure.

H9. The packaged PDF is not tagged

The PDF renders cleanly, has 17 pages and includes bookmarks, but structural inspection reports Tagged: no, no /StructTreeRoot, no /MarkInfo, and no document language. open_desiredgain_guide() and its Rd page explicitly call it “the tagged PDF.”

Fix: produce a genuinely tagged PDF with language and reading-order structure, or remove the accessibility claim. Add a release test for PDF structure if “tagged” remains promised.

H10. The published-data reproduction is only a partial identity check

The frozen numbers verify that published Pesek-Baker gains are proportional to the published desired-gain vector. The package is then tested on a different, internally generated covariance matrix. This does not reproduce published coefficients or rankings through DesiredGainR.

The article explicitly provides its datasets through BioStudies and publishes the Method 1 coefficients, so the claim that the calculation cannot be reproduced should be revisited. The package also cites the wrong article title: the DOI resolves to Estimating optimum and base selection indices in plant and animal breeding programs by development new and simple SAS and R codes, not the title stored in R/data-rahimi.R.

Fix: retrieve the archived matrices/data under their license, freeze their checksums and provenance, and reproduce coefficients, responses and rankings with explicit tolerances. Keep the current identity check as a smaller supplementary test.

H11. Desired-gain evaluation changes the definition of merit

For Pesek-Baker and Yamada, the package invents implied economic weights G^-1 P G^-1 d and then reports R_HI and aggregate merit under that derived objective. A different desired-gain direction gets a different definition of net merit, so these values are not directly comparable with Smith-Hazel or another desired-gain index under one common breeding objective.

Fix: when economic weights were not supplied, label these criteria as being relative to an implied objective and do not use them for cross-method merit comparisons. Prefer NA for net-merit criteria unless the user supplies a common aggregate_weights vector.

Release engineering and documentation issues

E1. CI hardening is incomplete

  • The lint step calls lintr::lint_package() but never fails when lints are returned.
  • The pkgdown workflow still warns and publishes when the guide HTML is missing, knowingly leaving a 404.
  • cran-comments.md claims 0 errors, warnings and notes despite the reproducible example failures.
  • The release checklist records failures but exits successfully and ignores notes in its clean-check decision.

E2. Citation and release metadata are still inconsistent

DESCRIPTION, CITATION.cff, inst/CITATION and .zenodo.json use different software titles. NEWS.md calls 0.5.0 “in development,” while CITATION.cff declares a release date and cran-comments.md describes a submission.

Fix: define one title/version/release status source and generate the other metadata. Add the software DOI only after it exists.

E3. Feature maturity documentation is stale and does not ship

MATURITY.md says versions “up to 0.5.0” have the DGSI unit defect even though this 0.5.0 tree contains the fix. It omits the new propagation and multi-environment functions and says the optimizer conditions only on fixed covariance without pointing to the new outer-loop function. It is excluded by .Rbuildignore, so installed users cannot read it.

E4. The upstream “adapters” are mostly a matrix validator

source is recorded but does not drive package-specific extraction. The ASReml named-vector parser recognizes only simple trait tokens split on [:.!]; real fitted-object variance-component names are often more complex. For sommer, breedR, BGLR and StageWise, the caller must extract the covariance matrix themselves.

Fix: describe this honestly as validate_covariance()/import_covariance() unless tested extractors for actual fitted objects are added.

E5. Remaining repository and method debt

  • The legacy example CSVs are excluded from the build but still remain in the repository.
  • scripts/build.R is a long interactive scratch script containing duplicate site builds, package removal, RStudio-only restart calls and references to unrelated old files. Replace it with a short reproducible build script.
  • bend_covariance() now reports ASRgenomics’ aggressive changes honestly, but it still offers only the method that changes trait variances and targets a condition number near 100. Add a trait-covariance-specific repair option or keep this explicitly experimental.
  • print.desiredgainr_index() reports the requested selected count rather than the actual count when hard culling returns fewer candidates.
  • The package still lacks a completed CRAN release, software DOI, submitted methods paper and independently reproducible breeding-program case study.

Prior findings now genuinely resolved

The following changes were confirmed and should be retained:

  • malformed Rd mathematics is fixed;
  • both guide editions ship, HTML is the default, and the source renders;
  • the hard-coded citation version was removed;
  • DGSI converts SD-unit gains before raw-scale solving and passes unit invariance tests;
  • classical theoretical transmitted response is reported separately from the empirical selected-candidate differential;
  • count and seed validation is substantially stronger;
  • simulation cycle 0/1 semantics are corrected;
  • SimParam state is deep-cloned and effective thread count is recorded;
  • marker identity mismatches now stop rather than silently falling back;
  • full clonal covariance calibration and clonal phenotype replication were added;
  • estimated-P compatibility status and override provenance are returned;
  • QTL segregation and marker-based relationship are reported separately;
  • duplicate optimizer pool points are excluded in the ordinary path;
  • S3 coef(), predict() and summary infrastructure exists, although the DGSI summary defect above remains;
  • source CI now covers R-devel, oldrel, minimum R, Windows and macOS; and
  • generated Rd files, examples, tests and vignettes otherwise pass.

Recommended repair order

Gate A — release and scientific validity

  1. Make both package checks clean and correct cran-comments.md.
  2. Replace the leaking DGSI holdout and all associated claims.
  3. correct/remove the Mallard and Harville implementations and citations.
  4. Make covariance propagation use residual draws, then add end-to-end tests.
  5. Repair the guaranteed-failing full-dependency CI job.

Gate B — optimizer reliability

  1. Replace the truncated fingerprint with a complete stable hash.
  2. Retain replicate outcomes/covariances and compute mode-correct uncertainty.
  3. prevent optimizer pool exhaustion loops.
  4. Fix named DGSI optimized directions and summary output.
  5. Make estimated-P compatibility unit-invariant.
  6. Make diversity defaults and disjointness guarantees internally coherent.

Gate C — expert-quality evidence and delivery

  1. Complete the real published-data reproduction.
  2. Make multi-environment stability operational rather than descriptive.
  3. Correct PDF accessibility, metadata, maturity and CI claims.
  4. Add real upstream adapters, a case study, DOI, methods paper and CRAN release.

Bottom line

The package has moved from a broad implementation-quality problem to a smaller set of identifiable scientific and release defects. That is real progress. However, the newly added restricted-index and covariance-propagation layers currently increase apparent breadth faster than validated breadth. For an expert-quality release, correctness and claim discipline should now take priority over adding further methods.
